channel.title: Members | GATAS Lab
channel.description: The members of the lab come from diverse perspectives with unique training. We are always looking for students and researchers with a desire to solve problems by leveraging abstract applications in novel science and engineering applications. We are hiring The lab is accepting PhD students, postdocs, research scientists, and undergraduate researchers. See how to join for what we are looking for and how to get in touch.

item.title: James Fairbanks
item.description: Principal Investigator Active ProgramComputational Science and Engineering DegreePhD In the lab since2021 Website GitHub James Fairbanks is an assistant professor in the department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, and affiliated with the Institute for Computational Engineering, and the Florida Institute for National Security. His research focuses on new paradigms in scientific computing, specifically applied category theory. This approach to mathematical modeling focuses on structure and structure preserving relationships between mathematical objects. The GATAS lab studies these topics and supports software-focused research in the AlgebraicJulia Ecosystem. We collaborate closely across the HWCOE and with external collaborators at NIST, AFRL, and the Topos Institute.

item.title: George Rauta
item.description: Graduate student Active ProgramCISE DegreePhD StagePre-proposal In the lab since2022 GitHub George Rauta is a PhD student with a focus in numerical linear algebra and high-performance computing. He believes that advances in the field of computer science are dependent on the existence of a highly performant computational foundation. It is critical that this foundation considers the theoretical aspects of algorithms, the method by which they are implemented in code and how they interact with the physical designs of modern processing and memory units.

item.title: Richard Samuelson
item.description: Research scientist Active In the lab since2024 Website GitHub Google Scholar LinkedIn Richard Samuelson is researching category theory, convex analysis, and high-performance computing. He has made significant contributions to the CliqueTrees.jl package, implementing the ChordalLDLt multifrontal factorization that underpins sparse symmetric positive-definite linear solves. These improvements accelerate nullspace and global-section computations in the CellularSheaves.jl library and enable more efficient compositional methods across the lab’s projects. Selected publications Graphical Quadratic Algebra – ICTAC 2025 (Lecture Notes in Computer Science). Dario Stein, Fabio Zanasi, Robin Piedeleu, and Richard Samuelson. DOI: 10.1007/978-3-032-11176-0_18 A Categorical Treatment of Open Linear Systems – Logical Methods in Computer Science, 2025. Dario Stein and Richard Samuelson. DOI: 10.46298/lmcs-21(3:11)2025

item.title: Joana Bou Barcelo
item.description: Graduate student Active ProgramMAE DegreePhD StagePre-proposal In the lab since2024 GitHub LinkedIn Joana Bou Barcelo is a PhD student in the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at the University of Florida. Her work combines the GATAS Lab’s compositional methods with nonlinear control. Her work applies cellular sheaves to coordination problems in multi-agent systems. In Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Multi-Target Tracking using Cellular Sheaves, written with Tyler Hanks, Cristian F. Nino, Austin Copeland, Warren Dixon, and James Fairbanks, the team poses the tracking of several unknown targets as a harmonic extension problem on a cellular sheaf. Because a sheaf can carry a different stalk over each agent, the formulation handles agents whose state spaces have different dimensions, which is difficult to express in the usual graph-Laplacian setting. The resulting decentralized controller is built from the sheaf Laplacian and comes with Lyapunov-based stability guarantees.

item.title: Itay Kadosh
item.description: Graduate student Active ProgramMAE DegreePhD StagePre-proposal In the lab since2026 GitHub Google Scholar LinkedIn Itay Kadosh is a PhD student in the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at the University of Florida, where he joined the GATAS Lab in 2026. His research interests are robotics, computer vision, and optimization, and in the lab he works on the control and numerical side of CellularSheaves.jl, the package the group uses to pose multi-agent coordination problems as sheaves. Coordinating a fleet on a cellular sheaf reduces, at every control step, to one linear system called the harmonic extension, in which a moving target changes only the right-hand side. Itay built the closed-loop model predictive control that drives multi-agent, multi-target tracking problems through that formulation. A tracking scenario is expressed as a time-expanded sheaf and solved as a quadratic program over the resulting trajectory space.

item.title: Samuel Cohen
item.description: Undergraduate researcher Emeritus In the lab since2024 GitHub Samuel Cohen is an undergraduate studying math and computer science. His work is implementing distributed optimization algorithms in the AlgebraicOptimization.jl package. This package uses the framework of category theory to exploit naturally occurring compositional structures in various optimization problems.

item.title: Matt Cuffaro
item.description: Research Software Engineer Emeritus In the lab since2023 Website GitHub Matt Cuffaro is the systems administrator and research programmer for the GATAS lab. He helps his colleagues build the AlgebraicJulia ecosystem, and is the custodian of the lab’s IT infrastructure.

item.title: Austin Copeland
item.description: Graduate student Active ProgramMAE DegreePhD StagePre-proposal In the lab since2026 Austin Copeland is a PhD student in the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at the University of Florida, where he joined the GATAS Lab in August 2026. He is co-advised by James Fairbanks and Warren Dixon of the Nonlinear Controls and Robotics group, and is working toward his qualifying proposal.

item.title: Liam Kunzendorf
item.description: Undergraduate researcher Active ProgramMAE In the lab since2025 Liam Kunzendorf is an undergraduate in the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at the University of Florida, and has been with the GATAS Lab since August 2025. He works with George Rauta on Decapodes.jl, the lab’s graphical tool for composing physical systems on the discrete exterior calculus.

item.title: Tyler Hanks
item.description: Graduate student Emeritus ProgramCISE DegreePhD StageGraduated In the lab since2021 GitHub LinkedIn Tyler joined the GATAS Lab in the summer of 2021 as a graduate research assistant and has quickly become one of the group’s most visible contributors to the lab’s work at the intersection of optimization, control theory, and machine learning. His research is driven by a desire to make complex engineering problems easier to specify and solve by exploiting the compositional structures that naturally arise in multi-agent systems, distributed optimization, and deep neural-network architectures. To that end, Tyler applies tools from category theory, abstract algebra, and type theory, which are areas traditionally associated with pure mathematics, to create rigorous, modular frameworks that can be reused across disparate problem domains.

item.title: Luke Morris
item.description: Graduate student Emeritus ProgramCISE DegreePhD StageGraduated In the lab since2021 Website GitHub Luke Morris is leading development on the CombinatorialSpaces.jl and Decapodes.jl projects, for representing multiphysics models and automatically generating simulations from those representations. He is interested in the problems that applied scientists face when they do any computational work. In particular, the problems of developing models faster, and of making the models themselves faster and more accurate. He leads a couple of projects on this front: Decapodes.jl and CombinatorialSpaces.jl.

item.title: Trevor Gross
item.description: Undergraduate researcher Emeritus In the lab since2025 Website GitHub Trevor Gross is an undergraduate junior studying computer science affiliated with the Florida Institute for National Security Talent Pipeline. His research interests lie in developing and implementing new techniques to solve existing problems. He works primarily in the AlgebraicOptimization.jl library, improving the efficiency of distributed systems and making other engineers’ work easier, and aims to contribute to research and to industry more broadly.

item.title: Wilmer Leal
item.description: Postdoctoral Fellow Emeritus DegreePhD In the lab since2022 Website GitHub Google Scholar LinkedIn Wilmer Leal is a postdoctoral researcher at the Computer Science Department at the University of Florida, USA. He is fascinated by the interplay between chemistry and mathematics, leveraging mathematical tools to solve chemical questions and using chemical intuition to inspire mathematical insights. His research revolves around developing categorical models for various flavors of compositionality in chemistry. As a chemist, he is naturally inclined to reason and navigate through reaction networks, which makes hypernetworks a particularly exciting area of study for him.

item.title: Benjamin Merlin Bumpus
item.description: Research Assistant Professor Emeritus DegreePhD In the lab since2022 Website GitHub Google Scholar Benjamin Merlin Bumpus was a faculty research scientist and led the algorithms subproject within the GATAS Lab. In 2023 he accepted a professorship at the Institute of Mathematics, Statistics, and Computer Science (IME) at the University of São Paulo (USP) in Brazil, where he now heads the CombTheta research group and the CUÍCA (Categorical Understanding in Computation and Algorithms) lab. His move to USP has expanded his collaborative network across South America and Europe, resulting in joint projects on categorical methods in computational complexity and graph theory. Recent highlights including the Brazilian Category Theory Conference and our paper on temporal data with sheaves being published.

item.title: Kris Brown
item.description: Postdoctoral Researcher Emeritus DegreePhD In the lab since2021 Website GitHub Topos Institute Kris Brown was a postdoctoral researcher in the lab from 2021 to 2022, arriving from a PhD in Chemical Engineering at Stanford. His work is on the implementation of category theory: how a categorical specification becomes a program, and how that program is made fast. He is the largest contributor to Catlab.jl, the library the rest of the AlgebraicJulia ecosystem is built on, and to GATlab.jl, which implements generalized algebraic theories and their models. He also worked on ACSets.jl, the data structure underneath most of the lab’s modeling tools.

item.title: Micah Halter
item.description: Research Programmer Emeritus In the lab since2016 Website GitHub LinkedIn Micah Halter worked with the group from 2016 to 2019 at the Georgia Tech Research Institute, while completing a BS in Computer Science at Georgia Tech. He was the research programmer on the group’s early compositional modeling libraries. The first of these was SemanticModels.jl, which studied whether a scientific model’s meaning could be extracted from its code and manipulated directly. That work led to AlgebraicPetri.jl, where he is the largest contributor. AlgebraicPetri is used to assemble an epidemiological model from parts: two reaction networks are composed, a model is stratified by age or region, and the dynamics are generated from the structure. It was used in the DARPA ASKEM program and in the lab’s epidemic modeling papers.
